page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c2.large is an x86_64 architecture server instance within the ecs.c2 family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated virtual CPUs (vCPUs) paired with 32.0 GB of system memory. This configuration establishes a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, allocating exactly 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance does not include local storage, requiring external block storage volumes for persistent data.

The hardware profile lacks integrated graphics processing units (GPUs) and complimentary public IPv4 addresses. This resource density makes the instance a dedicated compute-oriented resource. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the 1:2 resource ratio minimizes memory overhead expenses for workloads that are primarily bound by CPU execution. However, the complete absence of local storage means users must factor in the latency and cost of network-attached storage.

Given the dedicated CPU allocation and compute-heavy ratio, this server is designed for workloads such as batch processing, web serving, distributed analytics, and application servers that do not require high memory-to-CPU ratios or local scratch space.
